Character-Defining Features Character-defining features of a building are those that give the building its visual character and can be either exterior or interior elements (Nelson 1988). For the mitigation of 06-CP-65, the NNSS PA requires the identification of any interior character-defining features or spaces. Interior visual character can come from features of the building that are often important in defining the character of an individual room or space. These can be obvious features such as fireplace mantles or plaster ceiling medallions, but can also be items like hardware, lighting fixtures, bank tellers’ cages, etc. (Nelson 1988). Building 06-CP-65 was constructed as a warehouse with offices and laboratory space. As such, the large open warehouse space in the northern portion of the building is particularly distinctive of this function. This space can be divided by putting up chain-link fencing in various configurations. Four pairs of pedestrian double doors allow access into the warehouse from the loading dock, which fronts the east elevation. The east elevation also includes a single Nevada SHPO – ARA Form Page 3 SHPO Resource #: B18910 Rev. 2017 Other Resource #: 06-CP-65 metal-framed window that served as an ‘issue window’ for communication between personnel inside and outside the building. A large roll-up door is also present on the north elevation near the northwest corner of the building. Several specialized features are present within this space: two standalone adjoining rooms likely used for administration, a room-sized cold storage cooler that may have held undeveloped filmic media, and a high-pressure air workstation with fume hood. All laboratory space has been converted to offices which are today used as storage. 8. References Edgerton, Germashausen, and Grier, Inc. (EG&G) 1990 “NTS, Area 6, Bldg.
